title: Salford champions? Millers to spiral? - League Two club-by-club preview
description: BBC Sport correspondents assess the strengths and weaknesses of all 24 teams competing in League Two this season.
fullText:
League Two never fails to provide gripping entertainment right until the final day of the season.

If recent years are anything to go by, the 2026-27 campaign promises to be no different with Salford City tipped to win promotion to League One for the first time in their history and York City back in the EFL after a 10-year hiatus.

With Saturday's curtain-raiser upon us, BBC Sport spoke to correspondents across England and Wales for their takes on the clubs they cover and what to expect this season.

Follow your League Two club this 2026-27 season

Andy Bayes, BBC Radio Lancashire

Key ins: Joe Anderson (Barrow, undisclosed), Cole Stockton (Salford, free), Tom Moore (Southport, undisclosed), Louie Moulden (Norwich, loan)

Key outs: Ollie Wright (loan spell ended)

What are the expectations heading into the season? To achieve more points and a higher league position than they did last season. They made a three-point improvement year-on-year last season and flirted with the play-off places in early 2026 before injuries and squad depth took their toll.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? They have strengthened their forward line with the arrival of Cole Stockton, which has to help. Stanley will be hoping that he can return to the form that made him a wanted man during his days at Morecambe.

They have also brought players in from non-league football who will be hungry to show that they belong in the EFL. The club always has a 'never say die' attitude. They are always tipped for relegation in whichever league they play at the start of a season. That's of no interest to manager John Doolan or his squad.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Injuries and perhaps in some areas a little bit of inexperience could hamper them.

There are key players in the Stanley team that Doolan needs to get 35-plus games from this season - Shaun Whalley being a case in point. He missed the start of last season and was missed badly.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Shaun Whalley. Stanley's results with Whalley in the side are far different to when he isn't. He's a vastly experienced, talented player who his team-mates respect greatly. If he can stay fit for most of the season, they'll be fine.

Key ins: Oisin Gallagher (Lincoln City, loan), Matthew Cox (Brentford, loan)

Key outs: Ryan Glover (Stockport County, undisclosed), Callum Stead (Cambridge United, undisclosed)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Barnet were back in the EFL for the first time in seven years last season and finished eighth, just outside the play-off places. So minimum expectation is the play-offs, although the Bees have never been promoted via that route.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? The manager, Dean Brennan. No matter what the changes or challenges, he never leaves anyone in doubt about his aims or expectations. Plus defensive rock and leader Danny 'Mr Dependable' Collinge.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? The loss of some big players, plenty of new signings, and the need for those new additions to gel quickly with the team. Barnet have one of the smallest budgets, so Brennan's knowledge of non-league is crucial.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Tenacious, highly-skilled pass master Nnamdi Ofoborh is the conductor. Idris Kanu is the creator. Academy graduate Bright Siaw looks an exciting prospect.

Richard Hoskin, BBC Radio Bristol

Key ins: Kofi Balmer (Motherwell, free), Bobby Kamwa (Newport County, undisclosed), Reiss-Alexander Russell-Denny (Tottenham, loan), Tommy Leigh (Bradford City, loan), Richie Smallwood (Tranmere Rovers, free)

Key outs: Isaac Hutchinson (Doncaster Rovers, undisclosed), Kamil Conteh (Bromley, undisclosed)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Rovers ended last season so strongly under Steve Evans that supporters will be hoping to carry that momentum into the new campaign.

It's not gone unnoticed that a number of national pundits and publications are tipping Rovers for automatic promotion – and while a top-three finish is the expectation of most, experienced supporters will want the season to settle down before making any committed predictions.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? A number of players drafted in last January have returned to the club – Kofi Balmer, Tommy Leigh and Richie Smallwood. Defensively Rovers are strong, with a lot of players boasting previous promotions on their CVs.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? There's nothing drastically weak about Bristol Rovers. Some supporters have pointed out that the squad would benefit from the addition of a wide man, but that could well be addressed by the end of the transfer window.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? I've yet to see him play – but recent arrival Reiss-Alexander Russell-Denny could be a key addition to the squad. He'll be keen to emulate the impact of Yusuf Akhamrich, who had a successful loan spell from Tottenham last season.

Steve Kitchen, BBC Radio Gloucestershire

Key ins: Andreas Weimann - among a number of players with higher league experience.

Key outs: Bristol Rovers loanee - Isaac Hutchinson. He scored 15 goals in League Two, finishing with 18 goals in all competitions.

What are the expectations heading into the season? To build on the foundations that manager Steve Cotterill put in place last season. The 2025-26 campaign was about survival, with 18th place a fantastic achievement in the end. Many fans are talking about top half, with a shot at the play-offs if things click.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? After returning to Whaddon Road, with the club favourites for relegation last season, Cotterill reshaped the squad with contacts and hard work on the training ground. Cotterill brought the previously bewildered fans back on side, trusting and backing the manager and his players. That work continues this season with what looks to be a stronger, deeper squad.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Until the signing of Andreas Weimann, there was a lack of attacking experience alongside an exciting group of younger players looking to learn and strengthen their careers. Cheltenham will need them to settle quickly to life in League Two whilst finding the net, but it now looks like a well balanced squad on the available budget.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? It's easy to say Weimann but in reality there is no 'one player'. The key to Cheltenham's success will be Cotterill and tune that he gets out of a group of players that have joined the club because they've either played for him before, or have been enthused by what he's sold them.

From the kit design to the nets in the goals, he's involved in everything that happens at the club. It's no accident that he was (long overdue) given the keys to the Borough at the end of last season.

League Two fixtures: Your club-by-club guide to the 2026-27 season

Barnet 'better equipped' for promotion, says Brennan

Cheltenham sign striker Weimann on free transfer

Paul Fisher, BBC Radio Sheffield

Last season: 6th (lost in play-off semi-finals)

Key ins: Junior Eccleston (Sutton United, undisclosed), George McEachran (Grimsby Town, free), Jack Simpson (Leyton Orient, free), Alfie Pond (Wolverhampton Wanderers, free), Remeao Hutton (Gillingham, free), Fraser Bryden (Crusaders, undisclosed)

Key outs: Bailey Hobson (Harrogate Town, free), Armando Dobra (Leyton Orient, undisclosed), Jamie Grimes (Boston United, free), Janoi Donacien (Northampton Town, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Paul Cook has improved the Spireites in every single season he has managed the club, including the first time he was at Chesterfield just under 14 years ago.

Last season was disappointing that they could not reach the top three despite being tipped by many. This time, Cook and the fans expect promotion.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Defensively they looked to have strengthened, adding youth to experience, and pace up front will also hopefully be to their benefit.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Chesterfield conceded the most goals of any team in the top eight last season and still reached the play-offs. If they shore up at the back, top three will be achievable, injuries apart.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Liam Mandeville led Chesterfield's overall assists last season and was second in the table for League Two. If he's on song, then he could do it again.

Key ins: Sean Raggett (Rotherham, free), Thimothee Lo-Tutala (Hull City, loan), Bradley Ihionvien (Peterborough United, laon)

Key outs: Kyreece Lisbie (Reading, undisclosed), Arthur Read (York City, free), Matt Macey (Wycombe Wanderers, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? It's difficult to know exactly what to expect from Colchester United this season. The previous campaign ended with anticipation of a takeover being completed over the summer, but those plans collapsed in June.

Chairman and owner Robbie Cowling insists a competitive budget was always in place should the sale not happen, but it's not the renewed investment many supporters had hoped for.

Even so, Danny and Nicky Cowley have guided the U's to the fringes of the League Two play-off places in each of the past two seasons and have consistently recruited smartly within their means. If they can continue that trend, Colchester should again be capable of challenging in the top half and pushing for a play-off spot.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Colchester's summer recruitment looks sensible and solid. Sean Raggett and Paul Digby bring experience, leadership and physicality, while goalkeeper Thimothee Lo-Tutala arrives after a season playing League One football with Doncaster Rovers.

Perhaps more importantly, the U's have retained several key players. Highly rated left-back Ellis Iandolo has committed his future to the club, while influential midfielder Jack Payne remains. Last season's standout performers Jack Tucker and Harry Anderson have also stayed put, giving the squad valuable continuity.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? The biggest concern is a loss of pace and attacking threat in wide areas. Kyreece Lisbie's sale to Reading, coupled with the departures of Owura Edwards and Samson Tovide following the expiry of their contracts, has left gaps to fill.

Former players Bradley Ihionvien and Oscar Thorn have returned on loan deals, providing some familiarity and attacking options. However, Colchester will need to find goals from within the squad quickly if they are to mount a sustained challenge near the top end of the table.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Jack Payne remains Colchester's chief creative force. Operating in the number 10 role, he scored 13 goals last season, including two hat-tricks, and continues to be one of the most effective attacking midfielders in League Two.

Gary Smith, reporter, BBC Radio Sussex

Key ins: Vito Mannone, Jude Arthurs (Bromley, free transfer), Stephen Duke-McKenna (free transfer)

Key outs: Jacob Chapman (return from loan spell), Max Anderson (released), Josh Flint (released), Harry Forster (released), Harry McKirdy (released)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Most people will have Crawley listed as relegation favourites once again and after a relegation and a near relegation in the past two seasons, most fans will be hoping that the coming season is far better.

Having seen one pre-season friendly plus the game at Watford last week, my own expectations are that the side will surprise plenty of people and will comfortably finish mid-table or above.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? The strengths that will help them achieve that is that the head coach now has a squad to work with that he has put together himself as opposed to a squad that he inherited for the final seven games of last season. He now has the chance to impose his own coaching methods and style of play on the side.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? The relatively small budget that Crawley have in comparison to other sides could be the thing that holds them back. Having a whole new squad could be a great thing as mentioned but it also takes time for a squad to gel so hopefully this won't be a factor that prevents them getting off to a flying start in League Two.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Jude Arthurs. It won't be for his goalscoring prowess but more for his ability to knit the play together from his position as a defensive midfielder.

Pemi Aderoju who is on a season long loan from Peterborough could also a player to look out for. His off the ball running and his ability to get beyond the defence coupled with great pace could be the key to unlocking many defences.

Graham McGarry, BBC Radio Stoke

Key ins: Luke Offord (MK Dons, free), Joe White (Newcastle United, undisclosed), Jordan Gibson (Doncaster Rovers, free)

Key outs: Max Sanders (Notts County, free), Jack Powell (Hornchurch, free), Shilow Tracey (released), Louis Moult (Telford, free), Omar Bogle (released), Charlie Finney (released), James Connolly (Tranmere Rovers, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Crewe will have to defy the odds if they are to improve on last season and feature in what looks like being a competitive promotion race.

Rumours of a possible takeover in what will be the club's 150th anniversary have gathered momentum throughout the close season, but as yet nothing has been finalised, which will mean manager Lee Bell again having to operate with one of the smallest budgets in the division.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? While the recruitment of players will be limited, Bell and his staff look to have made some early positive signings which have been welcomed by supporters.

If the manager can keep most of his squad fit, which has not happened for the past two seasons, then there is no reason why Crewe cannot be dark horses to achieve promotion.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? The lack of strength in depth could be a problem, especially if injuries continue to hamper team selection.

Crewe need to show a marked improvement on last season's away form, which brought 11 defeats and only seven wins. At least another dozen points are needed if the Railwaymen are to be serious contenders for a top-seven finish.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? All the summer signings have brought some real quality to the squad, but if homegrown player Joel Tabiner can return with all guns blazing following his horrendous ACL injury that kept him sidelined for 12 months, he will make Crewe a stronger squad. The return of Tabiner will bring more creativity and goals.

Crewe can go under the radar for promotion - Offord

The League Two opening day fixtures in full

Taylor aims to bolster Exeter squad in coming days

Last season: 21st in League One (relegated)

Key ins: Josh Gordon (free), Gwion Edwards (Morecambe)

Key outs: Pierce Sweeney (Cheltenham Town, free), Ilmari Niskanen (Blackpool, free), Jack McMillan (Falkirk, free), Johnly Yfeko (Kilmarnock, undisclosed), Jack Aitchison (Bristol Rovers, free), Kevin McDonald (released), Josh Magennis (Stevenage, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Exeter City's delicate financial state saw a large number of experienced players leave. With the club relying heavily on a few free transfers and players from their academy, fans will be pleased if they can end the season in mid-table.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Exeter will hope manager Matt Taylor can galvanise the side in the way he did when Exeter won promotion from League Two in 2022. They will need to be tightknit and well-drilled.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? A lack of money and a lack of experience could be the key problem for Exeter. With last season's top scorer Jayden Wareham expected to leave before the end of the window, scoring goals could be an issue.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Jack Fitzwater. Exeter's new captain will have to lead a new and inexperienced side in what could be a difficult season.

Phil Gittins, BBC Radio Lancashire

Key ins: Danny Andrew (free), Jake Batty (free), Andy Cannon (free), Kane Thompson-Sommers (MK Dons, undisclosed), Josh Thomas (free)

Key outs: James Bolton (released), Elliott Bonds (Salford City, undisclosed), Harrison Holgate, Zech Medley (York City, free), James Norwood (released), Matty Virtue (released)

What are the expectations heading into the season? This is a difficult one to answer. The club have been clear that finance is not at the level it has been in previous years. The importance of a rich supply line from the highly respected academy to the first team has never been greater.

Recruitment over the summer brought both experience and potential. How quickly and well they blend will be crucial in head coach Matt Lawlor's first full season at the helm.

Difficult trips to promotion hopefuls Chesterfield and Grimsby await in August and will provide a better indication of where the Cod Army are at. It's very much a case of watch this space...

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Danny Andrew has returned for his third spell and alongside established squad members Ched Evans, Shaun Rooney and Jay Lynch, offers a depth of experience and know-how - vital commodities for all teams who are successful at this level.

Allied to those qualities, they are all well versed in the standards and expectations of the football club, which will be helpful to their youthful head coach as he looks to instil the right values into the younger elements of his squad.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Perhaps the biggest flaw within the make-up of the current squad is their frustrating propensity to ship late goals at the business end of games.

On nine occasions last season such lapses in concentration saw Fleetwood concede in the final 10 minutes. Worryingly this trait has already reared its head again in pre-season.

The club's progress will continue to be blighted until this trend is addressed, something that Lawlor is acutely aware of.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Having finished last season as the club's leading scorer, it would be easy and wholly accurate to identify Mark Helm as a key man for Fleetwood this campaign.

However, in an era when the importance of academy progression to the first team squad has never been more important, watch out for Crispin McLean - a young and talented midfielder, highly regarded by Lawlor, who to date has managed two goals from his seven first team appearances.

Key ins: Liam Gordon (Motherwell, free), James Brophy (Cambridge United, free), Will Goodwin (Oxford United, free), Ollie Wright (Southampton, loan)

Key outs: Sam Gale (Barnsley, undisclosed), Remeao Hutton (Chesterfield, free), Josh Andrews (Grimsby Town, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Back-to-back 17th-place finishes in League Two have certainly tempered the optimism of all but the most positive supporters.

The Gills' recent habit of starting seasons like they're going to win the league, then finishing with a whimper, also feeding a sense of pre-season caution around Priestfield.

Gareth Ainsworth has been given license by the owners, not only to stay on for a second season, but also to make upwards of a dozen new signings. Gillingham's success relies on what he's dubbed "his team" and "his era."

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? A mix of youth and experience - particularly in the new signings - could be the key. Scottish defender Liam Gordon looks just the sort of leader they've lacked at the back.

At the other end of the age spectrum, if defender Connor McManus, midfielder Zane Albarus and winger Sheldon Marshall make good on their considerable promise, it could be the season Gills' fans have (long) hoped for.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Having reached a club record 21-game unbeaten run in September, Gills' season fell apart.

In truth, they were weak in all departments. Fans and the manager are hoping that shedding 17 players over the summer, along with the new additions, will turn a decent looking side on paper into one that can take them into the top half and maybe higher.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? January acquisition Ronan Hale arrived for a substantial fee and with a prolific scoring record in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

If this new-look Gills squad can provide him chances, he could help turn them from underachievers to a real threat in League Two.

Matt Dean, BBC Radio Humberside

Last season: 7th (lost in play-off semi-finals)

Key ins: Iwan Morgan (Brentford, undisclosed), Andy Cook (Bradford City, free), Joe Foulkes (Kidderminster, free), Edon Pruti (Sutton United, undisclosed), Josh Andrews (Gillingham, free), Cian Doyle (Bray Wanderers, undisclosed), Harvey Cartwright (Hull City, loan)

Key outs: Jaze Kabia (Leyton Orient, undisclosed), Evan Khouri (released), George McEachran (Chesterfield, free), Tyrell Warren (Solihull, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? David Artell has improved the club each season that he's been at Blundell Park. After losing in last season's play-off semi-final to Salford, it would be a disappointment if the team didn't finish in at the least the top seven this season.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Grimsby were among the highest creator of chances and goals scored in League Two last season.

Their possession-based brand of football and philosophy of spreading the goalscoring responsibilities throughout the team might help make them a significant force again this season.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Uncertainty over the goalkeeping position. A lengthy summer search saw them miss out on main target Jackson Smith.

Harvey Cartwright rejoined but sustained an unfortunate injury which meant Christy Pym returned for their EFL Cup defeat to Blackpool, despite being made available for transfer this summer. It's the one position which has made fans jittery.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Iwan Morgan. The Welshman is hungry to make his mark after showing his promise playing for Brentford B.

Key ins: Harrison Biggins (Shrewsbury Town, free), Kyle Cameron (Bromley, free), Cameron Norman (Tranmere Rovers, free)

Key outs: Bobby Kamwa (Bristol Rovers, undisclosed), Matt Baker (Notts County, compensation), Courtney Baker-Richardson (Tranmere Rovers, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Avoiding another relegation scrap should keep County fans happy. Several positive pre-season displays, though, may have got some dreaming of a comfortable mid-table finish.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? A new, no-nonsense manager in Hayden Mullins who wants his team to play front-footed, aggressive football, not "tippy-tappy stuff".

Central midfield looks strong with the permanent signing of Harrison Biggins and the return to fitness of Wales international Matt Smith, while County have added League Two know-how in defence with the arrivals of Kyle Cameron and Cameron Norman.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Goalscoring could be a problem given County have dipped into non-league for a handful of forward players. Can the likes of Christian Doidge, Shaquille Gwengwe and Yahya Bamba deliver in League Two? A lack of pace in wide areas is another concern.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Biggins may have been discarded by Shrewsbury, but he should be the midfield lynchpin County lacked for half of last season.

He played a crucial role in Newport's successful survival bid after joining initially on loan in January, and could be the glue that keeps them together again.

What do Newport need ahead of League Two campaign?

Pato consortium set for Northampton Town takeover

Jake Sharpe, BBC Radio Northampton

Last season: 24th in League One (relegated)

Key ins: Matty Warhurst (Manchester City, undisclosed), Janoi Donacien (Chesterfield, free), Connor Evans (MK Dons, free), Lee Evans (Bradford City, free)

Key outs: Cameron McGeehan (Barnsley, free), Nesta Guinness-Walker (Aberdeen, free), Dean Campbell (Notts County, undisclosed)

What are the expectations heading into the season? It's difficult to say. Northampton Town are usually a big fish pushing for promotion in League Two. But the scale of the collapse of last season in which they lost their last 12 competitive games means a year of consolidation may be required.

Couple that with an exciting, albeit inexperienced, managerial appoint with Chris Hogg taking the reins in his first managerial role, anything mid-table upwards would be a success.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? The manager. He has a huge coaching pedigree which has been evident in how he has set this team up in pre-season.

There is fair amount of experience in the side as well. Jon Guthrie and Elliott Moore in the heart of defence are stalwarts at this level. Sam Hoskins is entering his 12th season with the club.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Final third quality. They have invested in striker Matty Warhurst who has shown his predatory instincts in pre-season.

But he needs a consistent source of supply and the supporting cast have yet to prove they're up to it. There is still time for a few more additions in those areas.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Again I'm going for Warhurst. It's a big call for a player with one senior appearance to his name. But very rarely do the Cobblers sign this profile of player and I've seen enough in pre-season to suggest he is capable of scoring goals at this level if he gets the opportunities.

Finding a goalscorer is the ultimate challenge and if Northampton Town have indeed found one then it could be the difference between success and mediocrity.

Josh Watton, BBC Radio Manchester

Key ins: Elliott Nevitt (Gillingham, free), Favour Fawunmi (Stoke City, loan), Ollie Norburn (Notts County, undisclosed), Ryan Delaney (free), Lewis Temple (Bolton Wanderers, loan)

Key outs: Tom Conlon (Tranmere Rovers, free), Jake Leake (Colchester United, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? In the words of Micky Mellon, promotion. He didn't shy away from the ambition speaking to BBC Radio Manchester.

Last season, Oldham went on a strong run and gave themselves a chance of making the play-offs, only for injuries to catch up with them at the climax of the campaign. This year, Latics will be hoping to go at least one step further.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Oldham have managed to keep the core of their squad together. Tom Conlon and Jake Leake both featured regularly last season and have moved on, but Mellon seems to have already found replacements for them.

Ollie Norburn is a really astute signing at this level, while at the other end of the pitch, the additions of the experienced Ryan Delaney and Republic of Ireland youth international Lewis Temple will add some much needed solidity.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Goals. Last season's top scorer was Jack Stevens with a total of five - a tally which isn't good enough for a side hoping to get promoted. There is a fear this could stump them again this time around.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? At 33, Norburn is one of the more experienced heads in the Latics squad and that could prove to be crucial heading into this season.

He helped Notts County navigate their way to League One last time around. Maybe he can do the same this year at Boundary Park.

Last season: 22nd in League One (relegated)

Key ins: Kyle Dempsey (Bolton Wanderers, free), Jasper Moon (Burton Albion, free), Jackson Smith (Barnsley, undisclosed)

Key outs: Jayden Stockley (AFC Wimbledon, free), Mitch Clark (Swindon Town, free), Ruari Paton (St Johnstone, undisclosed)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Twofold: Promotion and restore some faith in the team. Last season started with plenty of high hopes and ended with a relegation Jon Brady couldn't avoid despite improving performances as the season drew to a close.

After promotion campaigns in their past two seasons at this level, a top-seven finish is what most fans expect – especially given the investment in both the pitch and the playing squad.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Midfield and defence look strong. Both new goalkeepers in Jackson Smith and Mason Terry arrive with glowing reputations, while Jasper Moon, Lewis Montsma and Aaron McGowan reinforce a backline already featuring promotion winners Kyle John and Connor Hall.

Further up the pitch, adding Bolton's Kyle Dempsey to George Byers, Ben Garrity and Rhys Walters looks impressive business. Onel Hernandez's magic on the wing should also catch the eye.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? It's when you get to the final third that the reservations start to emerge about automatic promotion.

Mo Faal had an unproductive loan spell last season (but did arrive injured and without a pre-season) so questions have been asked about bringing him back. Oli Lynch is unproven at EFL level, Max Watters' career has stalled after a prolific spell at Crawley six years ago and Tyreece Simpson has been beset by injury problems.

Brady has pointed to bringing goals from other areas of the team, but fans are wary of the strikers' ability to score enough to secure promotion.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? A half-fit Onel Hernandez looked a class above at times last season, so when he proved his fitness in the summer to sign a 12-month contract, his quick feet, trickery and bravery on the ball should provide some entertaining football to get fans off their seats.

Michael Clarke, BBC Radio Manchester

Last season: 2nd in the National League (won play-off final)

Key ins: Laurence Maguire (MK Dons, free), Sam Sherring (MK Dons, free), Zain Silcott-Duberry (Sheffield Wednesday, free), Dajaune Brown (Derby County, loan), Jonny Smith (Wigan Athletic, free), Kaiden Wilson (Chelsea, loan), Nils Ramming (Brighton, loan), Cian Hayes (Peterborough United, undisclosed), Sam Waller (Harrogate Town, free), Jake Spaven (Wigan Athletic, free)

Key outs: Kyron Gordon (Stockport, free), Liam Humbles (Altrincham, undisclosed), Aidan Barlow (Altrincham, free), David Tutonda (Accrington Stanley, free), Tarryn Allarakhia (Boreham Wood, free), Tyler Smith (Derry City, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Survival scrap. With a new manager, a new system and some new signings, a season where Dale can consolidate their place in League Two is the primary objective, however they'll quietly hope for more.

After an impressive 106 league points amassed in the National League last season, and only narrowly missing out on the title on the final day, they showed spirit to gather themselves, reach Wembley and even overcome a 2-0 deficit in the play-off final to tie the game and eventually beat Boreham Wood on penalties.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? A young, hungry squad who will hope to utilise pace and width to provide plenty of service to Mani Dieseruvwe, who scored 28 goals across all competitions for Rochdale last season.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? It's early days, but so far Dale have struggled defensively with individual errors seeing them gift goals during pre-season and in their first two competitive matches of the campaign in the EFL Cup.

However, I think it's only fair to point out that we haven't seen what Ian Watson believes is his best XI yet, owing to injuries and players arriving who aren't fully match fit.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? While many will understandably point to Dieseruvwe, I'm looking forward to seeing more of Zain Silcott-Duberry.

He scored off the bench on his debut against Tranmere in the preliminary round of the EFL Cup and he has the potential to really excite the fans. If he can find consistency, the former Bournemouth man could be a real menace to defenders in League Two.

Rob Staton, BBC Radio Sheffield

Last season: 23rd in League One (relegated)

Key ins: Paul Mullin (Wrexham, free), Fabio Tavares (Burton Albion, free), Ossama Ashley (Salford City), Jamie Jellis (Walsall, free)

Key outs: Sam Nombe (MK Dons, undisclosed), Joe Powell (Salford City, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? I think a good season for Rotherham United would be one where they consolidate and start to build something for the long term. I'm not sure some of the fans, or more importantly the chairman, will view it that way.

The Millers have gone through managers as they drop down the leagues and they have not had a consistent transfer plan. They need to build something - even if that means accepting they might not be in the mix to go straight back up this season.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? A lot of responsibility is going to be placed on Paul Mullin to regain his best form. He is their high profile signing this summer. At the age of 31, it will be interesting to see if he can get back to the level that saw him help Wrexham move up through the leagues.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? They do not have a deep squad. Are they good enough across the various key positions to be competitive?

We've seen teams go into a spiral before - Chesterfield, Tranmere, Leyton Orient, Scunthorpe and others. Do they have enough about them to avoid a similar fate?

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? It has to be Mullin. He has the pedigree and history of producing goals. Aside from him, if Denzell Hall stays at the club, he has the kind of quality to create an impression.

Josh Watton, BBC Radio Manchester

Last season: 4th (lost in play-off final)

Key ins: Macaulay Langstaff (Millwall, undisclosed), Luke Molyneux (Doncaster Rovers, undisclosed), Abraham Odoh (Peterborough United, undisclosed), Joe Powell (Rotherham, free), Will Norris (Wycombe Wanderers, free), Will Aimson (Wigan Athletic, free)

Key outs: Cole Stockton (Accrington Stanley, free), Ossama Ashley (Rotherham)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Promotion. The message from the board couldn't be clearer - they want this season to be their last in League Two.

Karl Robinson was a popular figure among fans, but failure to beat Crawley on the final day of the season to finish in the automatics, followed by that play-off final defeat meant his time was up. Peter Cklamovski's task is simple - get Salford City promoted.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? The experience and quality of the squad. It's been a busy summer for Salford, with a number of players signed from sides in higher divisions.

The biggest of those names is Macaulay Langstaff, the forward joined from Championship side Millwall. They will be hoping he will be the one to fire them into League One.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? It's tough to pick out weaknesses from a side who finished fourth and reached the play-off final. It seemed last season mentality was a big issue.

They needed to beat lowly placed Crawley Town on the final day to achieve automatic promotion but failed to do so. They got all the way to Wembley and simply didn't show up. It's clear the quality is there, but the question is can they do it when it really matters?

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Macaulay Langstaff has already been mentioned, a proven goalscorer at this level, however fellow new arrivals Luke Molyneux and Abraham Odoh will be expected to contribute just as much in front of goal.

They have retained talent such as Kelly N'mai too, so I suspect they will be the entertainers of the division next season.

Nick Southall, BBC Radio Shropshire

Key ins: Joe Gbode (Luton Town, loan), Arkell Jude-Boyd (Cheltenham, free), Sam Proctor (Aston Villa, loan), Josh Davison (Tranmere, free)

Key outs: Matt Cox (returned to Brentford from loan), Iwan Morgan (returned to Brentford from loan)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Gavin Cowan's first job was to keep Shrewsbury in the Football League last season. He accomplished that as a head coach. He's now manager. A simple shift in job title but with bigger responsibilities.

Cowan's had the summer to bring in his own players without someone above him dictating who to buy. Town moved away from their director of football model in the early stages of last season after a poor summer of recruitment which cost Micky Moore his job and ultimately led to a relegation battle, with previous head coach Michael Appleton losing his job.

There are no such distractions for Cowan but he's faced with rebuilding a squad on one of the league's lowest budgets. A top-10 finish would be an achievement and a sign of real progress from where the club's found itself in the past couple of years.

I'm sure privately they'll want to push for promotion and with Cowan at the helm, you wouldn't write them off, but he'll have to work his magic.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Town's defence is their strength. Cowan has them well drilled and the retention of Luca Hoole and Josh Ruffels has been a masterstroke by the Shrewsbury boss.

Up and coming goalkeeper Will Brook has shown he has the quality to do well in League Two and he'll be competing with Aston Villa star Sam Proctor who's joined on loan. Arkell Jude-Boyd and Kevin Berkoe provide energy and pace as wing-backs.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Goals, or a lack of them. They only mustered 42 in League Two last season, the second lowest. Their defence saved them. Have they solved that problem this summer? Partly, but I'm sure they're still on the lookout for more options.

Josh Davison joins from Tranmere and he's hit the ground running with a couple of goals against an Aston Villa XI in pre-season. Joe Gbode, on loan from Luton Town, will be hoping he's the key to improving Shrewsbury's success in front of goal.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? That's easy, Will Gray. He's just signed a three-year deal, and he's destined for a very bright future in the game.

The homegrown midfielder wowed supporters with his elegance on the ball and a maturity beyond his years when given his chance to shine in men's football under Cowan. Gray has many suitors and he's expected to live up to the high bar he's already set.

Andrew Hawes, BBC Radio Wiltshire

Key ins: Mitch Clark (Port Vale, free), Joe Hungbo (Wigan Athletic, loan), Matty Virtue (Fleetwood Town, free)

Key outs: Darren Oldaker (Southend United, undisclosed), Will Wright (Barnet, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Expectations are surprisingly difficult to define. Last season's fast start but slow end and a pre-season that has suggested hamstring problems might be contagious have dampened, but not eliminated, hopes of a top-seven finish.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? Aaron Drinan's transformation from willing runner to League Two's top marksman was impressive and offers hope, as do signs of a clear high-pressing energy in pre-season.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Injuries are destined to really test squad depth, with midfield metronome Gavin Kilkenny and promising striker Fletcher Holman already out for long spells.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Swindon need centre-back Ryan Tafazolli to stay as fit as possible. His height and organisational skills were obviously missed when absent.

Chris Coughlin, BBC Radio Merseyside

Key ins: Tom Ince (free), Will Vaulks (free), Jordan Davies (free), Harrison Male (free)

Key outs: Omari Patrick (released), Kristian Dennis (released), Joe Murphy (retired)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Until Tranmere Rovers' takeover is completed, it's difficult to say exactly what the club's aims are. The situation off the pitch is far from ideal, with supporters growing increasingly frustrated.

On the pitch, Tranmere have finished in a lower league position in each of the past seven seasons since their relegation to League Two in 2020. They've been dangerously close to the relegation places in the past two seasons, including last year's great escape under Pete Wild when they survived on the final day.

With Darrell Clarke now in charge, Tranmere should be looking up and their EFL Cup performance against Rochdale showed plenty of positives for the squad to take forward. Overall, the aim will likely be to avoid any concerns of the drop this campaign.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? This squad has goals in it and it will need them to make up for Omari Patrick's departure.

Charlie Whitaker and Jordan Davies both scored in the EFL Cup preliminary round defeat by Rochdale, while there'll be a huge emphasis on former Watford winger Tom Ince after his surprise move to Prenton Park.

Joe Ironside is a proven forward at League Two level despite an underwhelming first season and defender Nathan Smith scored more goals than any other centre-back in the division last year.

Of course, they then have to keep goals out at the back but there is potential for exciting, attacking football this season.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? To put it simply, struggling to win football matches. In each of the past two seasons, only two teams have won less games than Tranmere Rovers in League Two and three of those four teams were relegated with the exception of Crawley who finished 22nd last season.

Despite a huge turnover in the squad between the two campaigns, that trend has continued which is undoubtedly a big concern. That's something that must change under Clarke if Tranmere are to progress.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? It has to be Ince. His arrival on a free transfer is a massive coup and statement of intent.

This is only the second season of his career that he's played outside the top two divisions of English football, the other being a loan spell at Notts County in League One in 2010-11.

He brings a wealth of experience and quality to the club, having played in the Championship for each of the past four seasons. He even scored a league hat-trick for Watford last season against Birmingham City. He'll be relied upon to be a leader on and off the pitch.

Key ins: James Connolly (Crewe Alexandra, free), Sven Sprangler (St Johnstone, undisclosed), Andy Dallas (Barnsley, free)

Key outs: Jamille Matt (released), Aden Flint (released), Brandon Comley (Barnet, free), Josh Gordon, Priestley Farquharson (Crawley Town, free), Connor Barrett (Wigan Athletic, undisclosed), Evan Weir (Peterborough United, free), Jamie Jellis (Rotherham, free), Charlie Lakin (Barnet, free)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Lee Grant's own expectations appear high. Supporters would be justified in being more guarded, and may remain so for some time even if the club starts well after the bruising experiences of the past two seasons.

But last week's win at Bristol City in the EFL Cup, with a performance that demonstrated organisation and energy – always a good early sign under a new manager – may raise sights.

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? The early signs are that the strength may be in the collective.

The switch of formation from the 4-2-3-1 of pre-season to a back three at Ashton Gate appears less significant than the apparent ease of the players in adapting to it, with their smooth organisation a feature. If sustained, Walsall could be more productive than the sum of their parts may suggest.

Although they are short on well-known names at this level, especially with Alex Pattison out of the picture for a while, there are several young players – Mason Hancock, Harrison Burke and Courtney Clarke among them – with clear potential to move their careers forward if this season goes well. If fitter for longer, Aaron Pressley can be an effective spearhead.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Like all teams with a young core in such a closely-fought league, progress may not always follow a steady upward gradient.

Some of their talented youngsters will prove themselves at this level, others will stumble, and it is not always easy to predict which. Their squad is also small enough at present to come under pressure – not only to protect against injuries, but also uneven form.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Courtney Clarke took a more scenic route to regular professional football than most with his talent, via South Shields and Eastbourne before his chance with the Saddlers.

His first full season at League Two level was up and down, and his longest run of league starts was only five. But there were enough examples of his ability – explosive bursts of speed from various parts of midfield and a spectacular goal at Norwich – to believe that with a year in the league behind him, he can start to produce those moments more often.

New EFL season gets under way... for four teams

York striker Stones signs five-year deal

York appoint Lindsey after shock Maynard sacking

Last season: National League champions (promoted)

Key ins: Scott Lindsey (head coach), Arthur Read (Colchester United, free)

Key outs: Stuart Maynard (head coach)

What are the expectations heading into the season? Until a couple of weeks ago, supporters were expecting a tilt at promotion with the owners openly admitting that if City didn't go back-to-back, they will have failed this season.

However, if they don't get off to a good start, the pressure will soon increase on new head coach Scott Lindsey and those in charge. Has a football club where there is disharmony in the background, ever been successful on the pitch?

After a summer of huge optimism, part-owner Matt Uggla's decision to sack Stuart Maynard, and not really explain why, has completely destroyed the positive atmosphere around City's return to the EFL for the first time in 10 years.

With rumours some players who were part of City's record-breaking squad not being happy with the change, how long will it take them to get over the shock of it?

What are the major strengths of the team to help them achieve that? The togetherness of the many players that remain from last season and the bond they have with supporters. They'll always give 100% irrespective of what they think about some of the decisions made in the past couple of weeks.

And what are the underlying weaknesses that could hold them back? Having to get used to a new system and a manager not knowing how to get the best out of the players he has inherited.

Brought in just a couple of weeks before the start of City's return to the EFL, can Lindsey get the players to reach the same dizzy heights Maynard got them to last season?

Of course it's not Lindsey's fault Maynard was sacked, but that didn't stop chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" and "Stuart Maynard's Barmy Army" coming down from the stands during the EFL Cup defeat by Crawley. If City don't get off to a flying start in League Two, they are likely to get louder.

Who's a player to look out for this season who could be a difference-maker? Striker Josh Stones. Superb last season. The £300,000 signing from Wigan 18 months ago has already been attracting admiring advances from other clubs.

But he's now signed a new long-term contract. However, if the goals start to flow, he'll be the next player to leave the LNER for a huge transfer fee.

title: Hammers & Boro to go up? Championship club-by-club preview
description: BBC Sport correspondents take a closer look at the 24 teams taking part in the 2026-27 Championship season.
fullText:
Here we go again... you can leave the Viking Row, Wonderwall, Mexican ducks and (most) hydration breaks in the summer of '26 - proper football is back.

The open road of the Championship season stretches nine months before us, punctuated by 46 twists and turns along the way.

Whisper it, but it looks like being one of the most open and competitive seasons ever in a division which is already known around the world for being ridiculously unpredictable.

Just four of the 24 clubs in the second tier have the benefit of parachute payments in 2026-27, newly relegated West Ham, Wolves and Burnley, while the other, Southampton, begin the campaign with a four-point penalty after the spygate scandal which cast a shadow over the climax of the last campaign.

Lincoln City take their place in the division for the first time since 1961 after their heroics in League One, while Cardiff bounced back after a 12-month exile as runners-up and Bolton join them in the Championship for the first time since 2019.

As Wolves and Blackburn prepare to hit the open road on Friday, BBC Sport correspondents across England and Wales break down the 24 teams and what - at this stage at least, given the transfer window remains open until 1 September - we can expect from them.

Jobi McAnuff from the BBC's dedicated EFL podcast 72+ also offers his predicted finishes in the table.

Fighting relegation & eyeing promotion? Championship set for six-team play-offs

How will relegated trio fare in the Championship?

Key ins: James Beadle (Brighton, loan), Dael Fry (Middlesbrough), Kristoffer Lund (Palermo), Jhon Solis (Girona), Luis Vazquez (Anderlecht)

Key outs: Kai Wagner (Philadelphia Union), Ibrahim Osman (end of loan), Jonathan Panzo (released), Tommy Doyle (end of loan), Kyogo Furuhashi (LA Galaxy)

Expectations? While many supporters expected play-off places last season, this time around it is a more realistic ambition. Indeed, entering his third season boss Chris Davies will likely accept that the expectation of the owners will be a top eight finish as a minimum.

Strengths? There is a sense of continuity from the second half of last season when the squad was revamped with younger, hungrier players. The likes of winger Carlos Vicente, midfield stopper Jhon Solis and striker August Priske will have all benefited from the experience they gained. Skipper Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann should be one of the more formidable central defensive pairings in the Championship.

Weaknesses? Any route to the play-offs will require a rethink as to how Chris Davies sets up away from home.
